comments.author: @BrendonBreeden
comments.text: Delta Works system in the Netherlands spans 1,000 kilometers with dams, dikes, sluices, and storm-surge barriers. It was built after the 1953 flood killed over 2,000 people. That's the kind of engineering that saves lives

replies.author: @VagariousTravel-868
replies.text: Exactly. The Delta Works is one of the best examples of learning from tragedy. After losing over 2,000 people in 1953, the Netherlands built a system that now protects millions. That's engineering with purpose—not just building something, but building something that matters.
